channel.title: La Señal — Español por input comprensible
channel.description: A serialized sci-fi political drama in Colombian and Venezuelan Spanish, engineered as a 365-day comprehensible-input curriculum. A Bogotá astronomer detects a signal that is not from Earth — and the fight over what it means begins. Starts slow and scaffolded, ends at full native speed. Voice references: OpenSLR SLR72/SLR75 (CC-BY-SA 4.0, © Google). Private listening feed.
channel.itunes:author: La Señal

item.title: Prueba y promesa
item.description: Day 30 is test day: El Flaco quizzes his 'audience' with five passages retelling the month's story, each faster than the last, fifteen questions in all. Score yourself with the sheet in the show notes — your result shapes Month 2.

item.title: ¿Y ahora qué?
item.description: The morning after: the data confirms a sky signal and a ground answer, and the team must choose between three dangerous options. The vote never finishes — four men get out of a grey SUV, and Sarmiento's phone call is three words long.
The night the whole network listens. At 3:52 the signal returns, louder than ever and everywhere at once — and then, from the llanos, don Ramiro's voice says the words that change everything.

item.title: La víspera
item.description: The night before the predicted signal. Everything that can be checked is checked twice, clouds gather over the llanos, and each member of the team faces the longest wait of their lives in their own quiet way.

item.title: La antena del techo
item.description: Camila's late-night insight turns one giant dish into many small ears: a cheap rooftop antenna anyone can build. The network multiplies it across the country, dona Marta charges rent in ajiacos, and an old friend climbs back up the hill carrying shame — and something borrowed.

item.title: El plan
item.description: With the ministry holding a copy of the data, the team races to predict the signal's next repetition and catch its echo red-handed. El Flaco is named chief of logistics, and Colombia's cousin network mobilizes.

item.title: La decisión de Andrés
item.description: At dawn on the observatory roof, Andrés finally tells Camila about Caracas: the lab he lost, the team that scattered, and the antenna his father built on their roof. Then he gives her his answer.

item.title: La nota de voz
item.description: Tía Chela sends the longest voice note in Maracaibo history: three minutes of neighborhood saga with a bomb buried at minute two. Suddenly Andrés's work permit is not just paperwork anymore.

item.title: El hermano de Julio
item.description: A friendly ministry analyst just happens to drop by doña Marta's stall, and lunch turns into a polite duel where nobody says a single true thing. Afterward, Julio has something to confess.

item.title: Demasiado cerca
item.description: The triangulation math is verified again and again, and the answer refuses to change: the source is inside the solar system, maybe closer than the Moon. Julio finally believes Camila — which is exactly why he wants out.

item.title: La triangulación
item.description: Three antennas, one 3:47, and a dog named Rayo: the night the volunteer network listens together. Plus: how three friends shouting in a plaza explain how your phone knows where you are.

item.title: Los radioaficionados
item.description: To locate the echo they need antennas they don't have, so Andrés calls on Colombia's ham-radio community — retirees, a nun, and a llanero named don Ramiro who trusts no one. Plus: the hundred-year-old internet.

item.title: El eco
item.description: Andrés's new receiver hears the signal twice — once loud, once faint — and the difference between a bounce and an answer suddenly matters a great deal. Plus: whales, submarines, and the science of echoes.

item.title: La Verdad Oculta
item.description: El Flaco's conspiracy podcast connects dots that were never supposed to be connected, and Camila has to make a deal. Plus: how to enjoy a wild theory without falling for one.

item.title: La visita
item.description: Two ministry officials arrive for a 'routine' inspection, and Andrés delivers the performance of his life. Plus: how to tell a rolo from a paisa from a costeño by ear.

item.title: El informe
item.description: Sarmiento wants one safe line in the report: 'unidentified interference'. Camila writes the truth instead — and in a Bogotá office with a view, someone reads it, underlines it, and reaches for a stamp. Mundo Real: a gentle comic essay on Latin American paperwork.

item.title: Los perytones
item.description: Over breakfast, Andrés tells the true story of the Parkes 'perytons': seventeen years of mysterious signals that turned out to be the observatory microwave. Everyone laughs — until they remember their own signal already passed every test the perytons failed. Then Sarmiento calls: Bogotá wants the routine report early.

item.title: Las explicaciones
item.description: Camila and Andrés list every boring explanation for the signal — satellites, planes, radar, a broken sensor — and design a test for each one. Andrés insists on adding a microwave oven to the list, and promises the strangest true story in radio astronomy tomorrow.

item.title: El favor
item.description: To rule out satellites, Andrés needs a favor from his old CANTV friend — and in Maracaibo, everything goes through Tía Chela. Her first voice note is four and a half minutes of family news with a bombshell buried at the end.

item.title: Doña Marta
item.description: Doña Marta's food stall feeds the observatory — and hears everything on the hill. Today her gossip is funny, until she mentions two strangers in a grey SUV who were asking about Camila.

item.title: La apuesta
item.description: Over breakfast at doña Marta's, two theories about the late signal collide — and turn into a bet with national cuisine at stake. Meanwhile, director Sarmiento has heard about the engineer's extra hours.
The dish is fixed, the coffee is hot, and three people wait in the dark for 3:47 AM. What happens next is five minutes late — and it changes everything.

item.title: Manos a la obra
item.description: Two days of repairs, one story told in pieces: Caracas, the blackouts, and the long road to a hill outside Bogotá. Then Andrés asks the one question nobody else thought to ask.

item.title: El venezolano
item.description: The repair company sends an engineer to fix the storm damage. He arrives with a toolbox, a thermos he guards with his life, and opinions about arepas. Nothing at the observatory will be the same.

item.title: La tormenta
item.description: A violent storm hits the hills above Bogotá, and the observatory pays the price. If the signal returns at 3:47, will anyone be listening?

item.title: Día 5 — «El jefe»
item.description: Camila takes the pattern to her director and gets six words she will never forget: we need funds, not ghosts. On the ride home, for once, she is the one asking the taxi driver questions. Plus: who actually pays for astronomy.

item.title: Día 4 — «Otra vez»
item.description: Night shift at the observatory. Camila watches the clock crawl toward 3:47 — and the sky keeps its appointment. Two occurrences is not chance. Plus: coincidence versus pattern, or how scientists decide what is real.

item.title: Día 3 — «El taxi»
item.description: Meet El Flaco: taxi driver, conspiracy podcaster, and the fastest mouth in Bogotá. Camila half-listens to his wild theories — until one sentence about the sky makes her stop smiling. Plus: why Bogotá is cold on the equator.

item.title: Día 2 — «La rutina»
item.description: Camila's upside-down life: sleep by day, empanadas at doña Marta's, night shift at the dish. She replays the recording and sees something new — and her colleague Julio has one word for it. Plus: why astronomers work at night.

item.title: Día 1 — «El ruido»
item.description: Astronomer Camila Rey works alone at night in a small observatory above Bogotá — until, at 3:47 in the morning, her computers record a noise that should not exist. Plus: what a radio telescope actually does (hint: it hears nothing).

item.title: Episodio 0 — Prueba de nivel
item.description: A 12-minute listening diagnostic. Five passages, each faster and denser than the last, each followed by three spoken questions. Score yourself with the sheet in the show notes; your result sets Day 1. Instructions in English; everything else in Spanish.
